summary.summary: Basildon's gross external debt reached £695.4m at 31 March 2026 (net £674.4m after £21.0m of investments), up £36.1m over the year, though it stayed comfortably inside its £825m Authorised Limit and £775m Operational Boundary (peak in-year debt £707.4m). The council carries meaningful exposure to its housing subsidiary Sempra Homes Limited — £55.0m of long-term loans, £7.9m of short-term loans and £24.5m of shares — and its legacy commercial property portfolio (Stevenage, Bath, Tunbridge Wells, Richmond, Northampton) is now worth £30.1m against an acquisition cost of £41.8m, with gross yield of 4.96% undershooting the 5% target. No Prudential Indicators were breached and no new PWLB borrowing was taken in the year; instead the council drew £171.0m of new short-term loans from other local authorities.

news_drafts.headline: Basildon forecasts £3.4m overspend as temporary accommodation costs spiral to £7.7m
news_drafts.lead: Basildon Council is forecast to overspend its general fund budget by £3.4m this financial year, equivalent to 6.8 per cent of budgeted spending. The overspend is driven almost entirely by temporary accommodation, where costs are forecast at £7.7m against a budget of £5.6m, a shortfall of £2.1m. On a more positive note, the council's investment income has significantly outperformed expectations. With average cash balances of £43.9m against a forecast of £15.5m, investment income reached £610k in the first quarter alone, already exceeding the full-year budget of £512k. The council's capital financing requirement, the total amount borrowed to fund long-term assets, has fallen to £777.4m from a budgeted £791.3m. Separately, planning fee income is forecast to reach only £48k against a budgeted £860k, and a transformation savings programme budgeted to deliver £766k in cuts is now forecast to cost money instead.
news_drafts.paper_title: Enc. 2 - Capital & Investment Strategy Q1 Report

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 - Budget Monitoring Detail by Portfolio
findings.headline: Commercial property income is underperforming; Out of Borough commercial forecast £722k below budget
findings.detail: Out of Borough commercial property is forecast to deliver £2.163m against a budget of £2.885m, a shortfall of £722k (25% adverse). The council also shows shortfalls in Garages (£449k) and Strategic Assets (£227k), indicating broader underperformance in commercial property income.
findings.matters: Shortfalls in commercial property income mean the council's income assumptions are not being met; this erodes the revenue available to fund services.
findings.figures: Out of Borough commercial: £722k shortfall (25%); Garages: £449k shortfall; Strategic Assets: £227k shortfall

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 - Budget Monitoring Detail by Portfolio
findings.headline: The Organisation Transformation Programme is forecast to cost £20k instead of delivering budgeted savings of £766k
findings.detail: The OTP was budgeted to deliver £766k of cost savings (shown as negative cost). The latest forecast shows it costing £20k, representing an adverse movement of £786k (102.6%). The planned savings are not materializing.
findings.matters: A transformation programme that fails to deliver planned savings means the council's efficiency strategy is not working; the £766k that was counted on to fund services is unavailable.
findings.figures: Budgeted saving £766k, forecast cost £20k, adverse variance £786k (102.6%)

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 - Budget Monitoring Detail by Portfolio
findings.headline: Planning fee income is forecast at £48k against a £860k budget, a shortfall of £812k (94.5%)
findings.detail: Planning fee income is now forecast to deliver only £48k compared to the budgeted £860k. This represents a shortfall of £812k or 94.5% of budgeted income.
findings.matters: A 94.5% collapse in planning income means the council is not receiving expected discretionary revenue and requires alternative funding sources or service reductions.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 - Budget Monitoring Detail by Portfolio
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation costs are forecast at £7.671m, £2.082m above budget (37.3% overspend)
findings.detail: The largest single variance in the budget is temporary accommodation, which accounts for 62% of the total council overspend. Costs are forecast at £7.671m against a budget of £5.589m, a variance of £2.082m or 37.3%.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation is a demand-driven service; an overspend of this magnitude indicates demand significantly exceeds what was planned and requires either additional funding or service intervention.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 - Budget Monitoring Detail by Portfolio
findings.headline: Basildon is forecasting a general fund overspend of £3.363m (6.8% of total budget)
findings.detail: The council's budget monitoring shows budgeted spend of £49.261m but a forecast spend of £52.624m, creating an overspend of £3.363m or 6.8% of the budget. This is a material variance indicating the council's financial plan is not on track.
findings.matters: A material overspend indicates the council's financial plan is not being delivered and requires mitigation, whether through reserve draws, service reductions, or additional funding.
